spec.claim_summary: Buy Bitcoin on a new 20-day closing high at least three sessions after the prior marker, with a stop below the trigger and exit within 2-6 bars.
assumptions: Timeframe 1d chosen because claim describes 20day highs/lows, next-day entry and candlestick intervals; claim never writes 1d explicitly.
Direction long chosen from buy entry wording; low-side 20-day low short signals left out to keep single-direction test.
NOT EXPRESSIBLE: exact stop placement below the signal bar's high/low price level cannot be expressed; using 2x ATR(14) at signal bar as proxy for below the latest high/low.
Gap rule interpreted as no new 20-day high in prior 2 bars, so markers are at least 3 sessions apart and a marker exactly 3 bars prior is allowed.
Exit window 2-6 intervals interpreted as time exit; 4 bars used as midpoint of 2,3,4,5,6.
Entry at previous 20-day watermark on next day approximated by standard close-signal next-open fill; close beyond prior marker is same as close above 20-day high.
Asset BTCUSDT from Bitcoin (BTC) on Binance exchange.

evidence.quote: The market makes a new 20day high or low
previous high/low marker must have been at least 3 trading sessions prior
previous high/low marker must have been at least 3 trading sessions prior
OHLCV historical data for Bitcoin (BTC) from Binance exchange.
Buy entry is placed on the next day at the previous 20 day high/low watermark
Stop entries for failed trades are placed below the latest high/low that triggered the signal
Profits/exits should be taken within 2-6 candlestick intervals

audit_majors: entry: Claim triggers on 'a new 20day high or low' with close beyond prior marker. Spec encodes only 20-day highs (close > highest_high) and drops all 20-day low triggers. Assumptions admit low-side signals were left out, which contradicts explicit high-or-low wording.

stop_atr_mult: Claim requires stop 'below the latest high/low that triggered the signal' - a price-level stop. Spec substitutes a 2x ATR(14) stop with searched candidates, disclosed as NOT EXPRESSIBLE proxy. Different indicator/level invented by compiler that changes loss per trade.
